Slack developer docs

# Build an app with a coding agent

Agents, apps, and integrations for the place where work happens. Pick how you like to build and have something running in Slack in minutes.

1. ### Give your coding agent Slack skills

   One install adds the Slack developer skills, plus the Slack MCP server in Claude Code and Cursor.

   ```
   /plugin marketplace add slackapi/slack-skills-plugin
   /plugin install slack@slack
   ```

   Run inside a Claude Code session.
   **Enable auto-updates**: `/plugin` > Marketplaces > `slack` > Enable auto-update.
2. ### Tell it what to build

   Pick a starting idea or write your own, then copy it into your agent.
3. ### Chat with your agent in Slack

   Your coding agent scaffolds the project with the Slack CLI, starts it with `slack run`, and you can message your new agent right away.

   [How the skills plugin works ](https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-skills-plugin)

Slack MCP server and developer skills

## Connect your AI tools to Slack

Give Claude, Cursor, Codex, and other agents secure access to your workspace to search, read, and post. Add developer skills so they know how to build on Slack.

Server URL `https://mcp.slack.com/mcp`

Remote MCP over HTTP with OAuth. Your workspace admin may need to approve it. No approval yet? Try it in a free [Developer Program sandbox](https://docs.slack.dev/tools/developer-sandboxes).

#### MCP server + skills in one step

Run in a Claude Code session. You will be asked to sign in to Slack.

```
/plugin marketplace add slackapi/slack-skills-plugin
/plugin install slack@slack
```

**Enable auto-updates**: `/plugin` > Marketplaces > `slack` > Enable auto-update.

[Connect to Claude ](https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server/connect-to-claude)

#### Only the MCP server

From your terminal. Then run `/mcp` in Claude Code to finish signing in.

```
claude mcp add --transport http --scope local slack https://mcp.slack.com/mcp
```

[Manual setup ](https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server/connect-to-harnesses#claude-code-cli)

**Then check it works.** Ask your agent: `Using Slack, summarize what my team discussed in #general this week.`

### Slack MCP server `your agent → Slack`

Your AI tool works in Slack: search messages and files, read channels and threads, send messages, and manage canvases and lists.

[Server overview ](https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server)

### Slackbot MCP client `Slack → your server`

Have your own MCP server? Connect it to Slack and Slackbot calls its tools in conversation.

[Bring your server ](https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slackbot-mcp-client)

### For admins

MCP connections go through the standard Slack app approval process, so admins stay in control of what connects.

[App approvals ](https://docs.slack.dev/admins/managing-app-approvals)

## What brings you here?

Examples of how to use these docs. Pick yours and skip the rest.

Not sure where to start? **Build your first agent** with your coding agent, the Slack CLI, or App Settings.

## Skip to the finish line

Working apps you can configure, deploy, and forget. Start one from the CLI, open the code yourself, or hand it to your coding agent.

### Starter Agent

A minimal agent to make your own, with the Messages tab and your choice of agent framework.

`slack create my-starter-agent --template slack-samples/bolt-python-starter-agent`

### Announcement bot

Preview, post, and manage announcements sent to one or more channels.

`slack create my-announcements -t slack-samples/deno-announcement-bot`

Integrate

## Send anything to Slack

Sent here from another product? Get a working connection in about a minute. No scopes, events, or tokens to learn.

#### Webhook URL in about a minute

Best when your tool has a field for a Slack webhook URL.

1. Choose **Install to Workspace** and pick a channel.
2. Copy the URL under **Incoming Webhooks**.
3. Paste it into your tool.

```
curl -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' \
  --data '{"text":"Hello from my app"}' \
  YOUR_WEBHOOK_URL
```

What gets created

```
{
  "display_information": {
    "name": "Webhook alerts",
    "description": "Posts Webhook notifications to a Slack channel."
  },
  "features": {
    "bot_user": {
      "display_name": "Webhook alerts",
      "always_online": false
    }
  },
  "oauth_config": {
    "scopes": {
      "bot": [
        "incoming-webhook"
      ]
    }
  },
  "settings": {
    "incoming_webhooks": {
      "incoming_webhooks_enabled": true
    },
    "org_deploy_enabled": false,
    "socket_mode_enabled": false,
    "token_rotation_enabled": false
  }
}
```

#### Sending your own JSON?

Start a workflow from a webhook, map the fields you send, and post a formatted message. Needs a paid plan and a flat JSON payload.

[Workflow webhooks](https://slack.com/help/articles/360041352714-Create-workflows-using-webhooks)

#### Build it as an app

Need buttons, threads, or replies? Post with `chat.postMessage` from a Bolt app.

[chat.postMessage ](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.postMessage)
